newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen stocks close higher, investors hold back.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen stocks close higher, investors hold back.

text.p: Shenzhen's A and B share indices ended up slightly on Thursday on a strong economic forecast, but brokers said institutions have put their buy orders on hold as they wait out the annual report season.
The B share index rose 0.59 points or 0.38 percent to close at 155.51 on turnover of HK$52.34 million against Wednesday's HK$55.25 million.
The A share index gained 4.83 points or 1.23 percent to 396.09 on turnover of 6.22 billion yuan compared with Wednesday's 10.81 billion.
The indefinite suspension of trading in Hainan Minyuan Agricultural Development Co, announced on Wednesday, still weighed on the A share market, some brokers said.
Authorities are investigating the company for alleged violation of accounting rules in its 1996 annual report.
Others said they expected the effect of the Minyuan news to diminish as investors digest the news.

"Authorities will probably pay more attention to annual reports now the Minyuan event has happened," Song Bin, analyst at Central-South Securities, said. "But the market mood is still buoyant given last week's strong economic target figures."
China on Sunday announced an 8.0 percent gross domestic product (GDP) growth target and a 6.0 percent goal for retail price inflation for 1997.
On the B share market, appliance maker Tsann Kuen was the best performer, gaining HK$0.08 or 2.09 percent to close at HK$3.90 on volume of 431,700 shares.
On the A share market, steel products maker Chengdu Lianyi, which listed 24.8 million A shares in Shenzhen on Thursday, ended the day at 14.44 yuan on volume of 11.3 million shares.
